clue.text: First course in Sarkozy-style hot air? (Stupid chap has sod all)

parts.note: gaz is the French word for gas, the hot air a French president would speak of

indicators.note: a stupid arrangement is a muddled one, so the following word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
sod all is nothing, which is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A sneer at French windbag politics, with a dim man left with nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Sarkozy was President of France, so his style of hot air is French: gaz.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazpacho is a cold Spanish soup, served as a starter, the opening dish of a meal.

clue.text: Horny thing, TV presenter needs energy to come in two directions

parts.note: Ant McPartlin, of the TV double act Ant and Dec

indicators.note: to come in means to enter, so one letter goes inside the pair that follows

parts.note: left and right, L and R
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A randy TV host needs the energy to perform both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo. Energy sits between the two directions.
explanation.definitionFit: An antler is the branched bony growth on a deer's head, a horn-like thing, hence playfully horny.

clue.text: Holding back sailor doing a Clinton with a dress?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman

parts.words: doing a Clinton with a dress
parts.note: Bill Clinton's stain on Monica Lewinsky's blue dress was evidence in the 1998 scandal

explanation.surface: A sailor behaving as Bill Clinton did with Monica Lewinsky's dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits ironically beside the scandal: what Clinton did was the opposite of holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining means refraining or restraining oneself from doing something, so holding back is a synonym.

clue.text: Brenda's residence is out of soothing cream for one type of sex

indicators.note: something out of a place has left it, so one word is removed from the other

parts.note: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; Balmoral is her Scottish castle
a balm is a soothing ointment

explanation.surface: The Queen's home has run out of lotion needed for a certain kind of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II. Take the balm off the front of her castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral sex is a category of sexual activity, so one type of sex describes it.

clue.text: Sickly, but not dead, Lib Dem party's centre on the rise — prepare for physical action

indicators.note: something sickly is in poor shape, so the letters are thrown out of order
dead is abbreviated D, and not means it is taken away

parts.note: taken as written; dead's D then drops out

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the five
rising is going up

explanation.surface: A jibe at the ailing Liberal Democrats, whose party centre is rising before a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The D of Lib Dem goes, the remaining letters plus the R from party are mixed, and UP follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To limber up is to stretch and warm the muscles before exercise or exertion.

clue.text: Firm, in the grip of pure excitement — get back!

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other
excitement stirs things up, so the letters of the word before it are agitated

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A company caught up in sheer frenzy is told to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get back!' sounds like a shouted command to retreat, but it means recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to regain or recover money or losses, which is getting them back.

clue.text: Vain fantasist: one to catch in Private Eye

indicators.note: in places the words before it inside the setting that follows

parts.note: the magazine speaks of itself in the editorial first person plural
an means one
to nab is to catch or arrest

explanation.surface: A vain dreamer is just the sort of person Private Eye loves to catch out.
explanation.walkthrough: A reading of Private Eye as its editorial WE is the likeliest; the clue also works as a nod to the magazine lampooning pretentious types.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe is someone who longs to be famous or important, a vain dreamer imagining a status they lack.

clue.text: Swelling bishop, one squeezed by device

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: something squeezed by another is pressed inside it

parts.note: a device in the sense of a trick or stratagem
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bishop with a swelling, someone caught in a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Device means a trick here, not a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise is an injury where the skin discolours and often swells, so a swelling stands for it.

clue.text: (& 14ac.) Light caning tip: if oil is deployed it's a constant behind-the-scenes feature of our parties

definitions.text: a constant behind-the-scenes feature of our parties

indicators.note: deployed troops are spread out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: every letter of these five words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Kinky advice about a gentle caning with oil, apparently a staple of party politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The parties are political parties, though the surface suggests the other sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Political infighting is the squabbling between factions within a party, which goes on constantly out of public view.

clue.text: (+ 25dn.) Shadow member's first to get a drink

parts.note: member in the sense of penis, put first
to tail someone is to shadow them

explanation.surface: A shadow cabinet member is the first to be handed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Shadow suggests the opposition's front bench, and member a politician; read member's first as the member coming before the shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a mixed alcoholic drink, so it is one example of a drink.

clue.text: see 16dn.
Just look at that soldier, one sniffing round Brenda?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a soldier caught sniffing around the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for Queen Elizabeth II, famous for her pet dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen kept Pembroke Welsh corgis all her life, so a corgi is a dog nosing round her.

clue.text: Currie, hyper, getting end away, dropping Es: "flipping happy as a lark!"

indicators.note: flipping things over throws them out of their order
getting the end away means the final letter of the word before is removed
dropping means letting go of, so every E is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Edwina Currie, high on drugs and sex, declares herself thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting your end away is British slang for having sex, and dropping Es is taking ecstasy pills; here they remove the R ending hyper and both Es.
explanation.definitionFit: Chirrupy means cheerful and lively, like a chirping bird, as a lark is proverbially happy.

clue.text: see 9ac.
Bedroom variation of duo involving biro

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters come in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple's bedroom game with a ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: A biro is a ballpoint pen, a British brand name used for any such pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A boudoir is a woman's private bedroom or dressing room.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) "Do me a body so, with Kate's top wobbling," as ordered by William

definitions.note: a description of the record rather than a noun for it

indicators.note: wobbling letters are unsteady and fall into a new order

parts.note: every letter of the quoted words, taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Kate

explanation.surface: A lewd request whispered to Kate, apparently at Prince William's command.
explanation.walkthrough: William suggests the Prince married to Kate, but it is William the Conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror commissioned the Domesday Book in 1085 as a survey of land in England.

clue.text: A less busy time to see Dicky climax?

definitions.note: the answer is usually an adjective, used here as a noun phrase

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, as is off
a peak is a high point

explanation.surface: A quieter moment to watch someone reach orgasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a ribald word, but it is British slang for poorly or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak refers to times of lower demand, when trains or phone lines are quieter.

clue.text: Spectators induce shakes in hospital

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the hospital department

parts.note: A&E, the accident and emergency department

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Something brings on the shakes in a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is the group of people watching a performance, so spectators collectively.

clue.text: Make out some ass? No, goolies

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: running across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A crude question of which body parts to fondle.
explanation.walkthrough: Goolies is British slang for testicles; make out is a phrase for kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: To snog is British slang for kissing passionately, which is what making out means.

clue.text: Male interrupting Cat Deeley's closing piece could well be fired

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one letter goes inside the word after

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
M is the abbreviation for male

indicators.note: the closing of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of Deeley
piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A man butting in on a TV presenter's sign-off might get the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat Deeley is a British TV presenter, so Cat looks like her first name. Fired suggests dismissal, but the definition means shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tommy gun is a Thompson submachine gun, a weapon that is fired.

clue.text: Alternative talk medium coming

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
to gas is to chatter
M is the clothing size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A different kind of chatter, delivered through a psychic medium who is arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming is slang for reaching sexual climax, so the noun for that climax fits it, loosely.

clue.text: Try tossing Dan the sperm-producer

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: tossing throws things about, so the letters of the name are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to try pleasuring Dan, the sperm producer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing doubles as British slang for masturbating, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A gonad is a reproductive gland; the male gonad, the testis, makes sperm.

clue.text: Remake of "Noel houses party" upset old duffer

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word is read the other way
something that houses another holds it inside
a remake is a version made anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A revived Noel Edmonds show, Noel's House Party, upsets an old fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel's House Party was a 1990s BBC Saturday TV show hosted by Noel Edmonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an old-fashioned word for a silly person, a fool or duffer.

clue.text: Urges which were the downfall of publicity-seeking junior minister

definitions.meaning: first meaning: encourages, as in egging someone on

definitions.text: which were the downfall of publicity-seeking junior minister
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Edwina Currie resigned as junior health minister in 1988 after claiming most British egg production had salmonella

explanation.surface: Desires that brought down an attention-loving junior politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Urges looks like a noun about lust, but it is a verb; Currie's salmonella remark cost her her job.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to encourage them; and eggs, through the salmonella row, ended Currie's ministerial career.

clue.text: Pissed with Cable's balancing act support?

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, as is pissed in Britain
a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: Drunk alongside Lib Dem Vince Cable during his political balancing act.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable was a leading Liberal Democrat; in Britain, pissed means drunk rather than angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is the taut wire or rope on which an acrobat walks, holding up the balancing performer.

clue.text: see 10dn.
He purged smear surrounding Clegg's no. 2

indicators.note: surrounding puts the first word around the selected letter

parts.note: a smear is a mark or stain

indicators.note: number two is the second letter of the name

parts.note: the second letter of Clegg

explanation.surface: A smear campaign around Nick Clegg's deputy, cast as a political purge.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats, so his number two suggests a deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ran the Great Purge, killing or jailing perceived enemies in the 1930s Soviet Union.

clue.text: Bank's chief brought into open is to get rid of bung?

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside the next word

parts.note: to unlock is to open

indicators.note: the chief letter of a word is its first

parts.note: the first letter of bank

explanation.surface: A bank boss's bribe being exposed and dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: Bung is British slang for a bribe, which fits the banking surface, but here it means a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: To unblock something is to clear an obstruction, like removing a bung from a hole.
